quarterly_data.signal: Q4 AND FY2026 PROFIT DETAIL (CFO Hilary Maxson): Q4 non-GAAP operating income increased 22% in US dollars to $8.6 billion; the operating margin increased slightly while the gross margin declined, driven by the ramp-up of data centers and the acceleration in infrastructure revenue, more than offset by lower operating costs (starting with sales and marketing) from efficiency actions. Q4 non-GAAP EPS growth of 24% was partly due to a one-time net gain on investment; excluding it, non-GAAP EPS increased by 20%. FY2026 non-GAAP EPS was up 27% to $7.63 including one-time gains on investment, $6.83 excluding them. FY2026 gross margin stepped down around five points, as expected, from the infrastructure build-out and the acceleration in its revenues, primarily offset by lower operating costs as a percentage of revenue. The FY2026 net cash outlay for capital expenditures of $48 billion takes into account prepayments and timing impacts of around $8 billion. She said the RPO is 'all supported by long-term contractual customer commitments'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 non-GAAP operating income $8.6 billion (+22%); FY2026 non-GAAP EPS $7.63 ($6.83 excluding one-time gains); FY2026 prepayments and timing impacts around $8 billion

quarterly_data.signal: FY2027 AND Q1 GUIDANCE (CFO Hilary Maxson): FY2027 gross margins will step down due to the timing of the ramp-up of data-center projects into their full revenue contribution plus mix impacts, and she expects margin performance in infrastructure 'to improve rapidly as we reach full contractual revenue levels at our data centers'; operating costs are expected to be slightly negative year over year in dollar terms from efficiency actions; FY2027 total revenue growth of +34% in constant currency, surpassing the five-year revenue CAGR in the long-term outlook; FY2027 non-GAAP EPS of $8.05, up 18% in constant currency, excluding the net one-time investment gains booked in FY2026 from Ampere and Bloom Energy. Q1 FY2027: total revenue growth of between 27% and 29% in US dollars (cloud revenue +58% to 64%) and non-GAAP EPS of between $1.72 and $1.76, up 17% to 20%; she anticipates revenues and earnings will accelerate in the second half as further megawatts come online. Capex: FY2027 expected net cash outlay for capital expenditures of around $70 billion; customer prepayments and timing impacts are expected at around $20 billion-$25 billion, so reported capex will be higher by this amount (in the Q&A: 'just associated with third-party manufacturers. Not vendor financing'); she says these investments are driven by committed customer demand reflected in the record RPO.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 FY2027 revenue +27% to 29%, non-GAAP EPS $1.72-$1.76; FY2027 revenue +34% in constant currency, non-GAAP EPS $8.05; FY2027 net cash capex around $70 billion

quarterly_data.signal: DEMAND, COMPETITION AND THE CONTRACT MODEL (co-CEO Clay Magouyrk, Q&A): 'several years in, there's still a massively higher demand than there is supply'; more entrants will try to meet it - 'I don't worry about that' - and his focus is meeting as much of that demand as possible at a reasonable margin profile. Renewals depend on the multi-year service relationship, and over time he sees ways for Oracle to earn 'higher and higher margins' while offering 'lower and lower prices' as R&D makes operations more efficient. 'There will be many winners named, our strategy is to have them all as customers'; the infrastructure is 'fundamentally multi-tenant' and capacity is continually allocated between customers. He cannot say what the future mix of bring-your-own-hardware, prepaid and Oracle-funded deals will be ('an evolving business model'); customers contract with Oracle to get data centers constructed and designed, secured, networked and run as a cloud with general-purpose compute, storage, load balancers, security and identity around the accelerators. On Q4 capex: any increase that is not due to component prices is 'largely around timing' and he does not see it as related to component prices, while memory, SSD and hard-drive prices 'have definitely gone up'.

SITE CONTRACTING DATES (co-CEO Clay Magouyrk): of the five largest sites, Shackelford, Texas was contracted in August 2025, Dona Ana County, New Mexico in September 2025, Saline, Michigan in October 2025 and Port Washington, Wisconsin in September 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: contracted August 2025 (Shackelford), September 2025 (Dona Ana County, Port Washington), October 2025 (Saline)

quarterly_data.signal: APPLICATIONS AND DATABASE CUSTOMERS (co-CEO Mike Sicilia): Oracle took thousands of customers live in Q4, over 300 in Fusion alone; the VA electronic health record rollout added four medical centers in Michigan in Q4 and another four in Ohio in early June. Named Q4 customers: Exelon (utilities platform), Wright County Sheriff's Office (Public Safety Suite), Westfield Insurance (Fusion ERP) and Piraeus Bank (Oracle Banking); Claro, a major Latin American telecommunications provider, chose OCI, Field Services applications and the Oracle AI Data Platform to automate customer service for its 30 million subscribers; UK National Health Service Shared Business Services and QXO combined Oracle infrastructure or database products with Oracle applications; Vodafone selected OCI Dedicated Region in its data centers, the multi-cloud database offering in a partner cloud and Oracle applications to reduce costs and run processes faster, 'in some cases up to 60% faster'. New database AI features released: Oracle AI Agent Memory and Oracle Deep Data Security. On the 'SaaS apocalypse', he said 'maybe a couple quarters ago' there were some delayed decision cycles, but in mission-critical systems customers 'have quickly moved on', and he expects applications to continue to be a healthy contributor.
quarterly_data.figure: over 300 Fusion customers live in Q4; Claro 30 million subscribers; Vodafone processes up to 60% faster
